course_name_original: COMPUTER AIDED ANALYSIS OF MECHANICAL SYSTEMS
course_name_en: COMPUTER AIDED ANALYSIS OF MECHANICAL SYSTEMS
prerequisites: Fundamentals of Computer Science and Programming

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the operation, purpose, and expected performance of mechanical devices used in engineering, ranging on different topics that can be grouped in the macro-category of machine mechanics.
Critically transfer fundamental engineering tools in the analysis and synthesis of articulated mechanical systems.
Geometric modeling of three-dimensional mechanical systems using CAD software.
Dynamic modeling of articulated mechanical systems using the multibody approach.
Design simple open-loop and closed-loop control strategies.

Design the functional logic of a mechanical system, analyze its dynamics, model its parts to CAD and interface CAD models with tools for the automatic acquisition of geometric and inertial characteristics for the simulation of dynamics and control of systems.

Stimulate autonomous judgment on the comparison between engineering solutions both in the field of functional design and in the subsequent geometric and dynamic computer modeling of unconventional solutions for the typical problems of machine mechanics.

Present and discuss solution to the problem proposed as the theme of the final exam, as well as define in the oral exam the theoretical methodologies used to solve the thematic problem both in terms of the model of the dynamic system under examination, from the geometric (CAD), functional (operation, assembly, disassembly, rough sizing), and in its subsequent implementation to the computer (system simulation).
Apply and update the knowledge acquired to contexts other than those presented during the course, considering technological progress.
Use other CAD/MBS modeling tools once the operating logic is acquired.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the Mechanics of Multibody Systems and the Analysis and Synthesis of Mechanical Articulated Systems Assisted by Calculator
Static and Dynamics of 2D and 3D Rigid Bodies
Techniques of Derivation of the Equations of Motion and Linearization
Elements of Linear Control Theory and PID Controllers
Elements of Design and Construction of Control Systems with Ultrasonic Sensors, DC Motors, and Inertial Platforms
Basic elements of machines and mechanisms
Mechanical constructions, connections, and systems for the transfer of mechanical energy
Modeling of assemblies and function tests, assembly, and disassembly
Design and development of the final draft
teaching_methods: Classes in the classroom and/or at a distance using slides and/or notes
Lessons involving the use of a computer and a CAD system
Exercises and simulations to be carried out both by hand and computer
Laboratory exercises concerning the analysis of complex mechanical systems
assessment_rules: The assessment involves the discussion of a final project, which is compulsory to pass the test, followed by a mandatory oral test. The minimum grade (18/30) is achieved by demonstrating adequate knowledge of all theoretical aspects and developing at least a complete subset of the final project. The maximum grade (30/30) is awarded for excellent knowledge of all aspects during both the project discussion and oral examination. Praise is awarded for complete and significant mastery of theoretical and applicative content, high language skills, synthesis skills, autonomous processing skills, and ability to extend to industrial areas.
